New study raises big questions about taurine as anti-aging supplement
College student discovers psychedelic fungus that eluded LSD inventor
However, "much additional work will be required to take these findings forward in a way that will reveal whether or not the findings are applicable and adaptable for human health," Thompson said.
Recently, studies have explored psilocybin's therapeutic potential for treating various conditions, such as
anxiety
,
depression
and neurodegenerative disorders like
Alzheimer's disease
. Some of this research has led to clinical trials
with promising results
. But researchers haven't yet pinned down exactly how the psychedelic achieves its benefits.
One theory, dubbed the "
psilocybin-telomere hypothesis
," proposes that
psilocybin
preserves the length of telomeres, the protective caps of repetitive DNA sequences located at the ends of chromosomes. Researchers have long understood that
telomeres shorten with age
, and the rate of that shortening correlates to the rate of aging.
Related:
'Magic mushroom' compound creates a hyper-connected brain to treat depression
Sign up for the Live Science daily newsletter now
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
So if psilocybin protects telomere length, could it also delay aging?
To find out, study senior author
Dr. Louise Hecker
, an associate professor at Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, and colleagues administered different doses of
psilocin
, which psilocybin gets broken down into in the body, to isolated human lung and skin cells. The team found that the psilocin extended the lifespans of the cells by up to 57%, depending on the dose given.
The psilocin also preserved the cells' telomere length and reduced levels of
oxidative stress
, or the buildup of reactive molecules. Simultaneously, it led to higher levels of
Sirt1, a protein associated with longevity
.
On the left, the old mice not given psilocybin are shown at two time points in the study. On the right, the images demonstrate how mice given the drug grew back fur where they were once balding, and they also grew brown fur where they were once greying, as indicated by the arrows.
(Image credit: Kato et al. (2025). npj Aging.)
In short, the psilocin made the cells appear like younger cells, Hecker told Live Science. Hecker's research involves looking at the impacts of aging on the body, and everything she knew to test for "just worked" she said. "I was floored by the data."
The team then went on to study the effects of psilocybin on approximately 19-month-old female mice — which, in human years, would be in their early 60s. The mice received monthly doses of psilocybin for 10 months. At the end of that period, 80% of the treated mice were still alive, compared with only 50% of an untreated group. The treated mice also displayed hair growth where they'd previously had bald spots, and their once-white hair grew back brown.
"It's exciting that we can give this intervention in late life and have such a dramatic impact," Hecker said.

Psychedelics, in general, are known to
alter the workings of the immune system
and the body's
stress resilience
, both of which can affect organ health, Thompson said. "What is new in this study is the provocative suggestion that changes in the length of telomeres — important regulators of DNA replication — may be produced by psychedelics."

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理工具的应用潜力、安全性、错误处理及用户体验

不同观点：
• twalkz：认为AI代理工具能完成90-95%的工作，节省大量时间，但剩下的5-10%错误，尤其是细微错误，可能需要大量时间去修正和处理。这尤其在处理复杂任务和个人数据时会带来麻烦。
• 2oMg3YWV26eKIs：关注安全风险，尤其是代理工具访问个人数据（如邮件和日历）时的隐私泄露风险。特别指出提示注入（prompt injection）可能导致代理执行恶意操作，如泄露私人信息或未经授权进行购买。
• AgentMatrixAI：对AI代理从90%到99%的准确度提升持怀疑态度，认为这是LLM代理的经典"最后一公里问题"。认为许多演示隐藏了真实应用中的问题，过度炒作可能导致对代理工具能力的误解。
• pants2：提到OpenAI的Operator工具在一些网站（如LinkedIn和Amazon）上被封锁，担心代理工具普及后也会面临类似问题，需要通过代理配置等方式解决。
• bredren：讨论了AI代理在保持会话持久性方面的技术挑战，以及如何通过云实例和权限管理等方式解决。认为OpenAI在优化用户体验（UX）方面做得很好，可能吸引非开发者用户。
• ddp26：引用AI 2027团队的预测，认为AI代理在2025年中期会初步亮相，但目前仍难以获得广泛使用。
• alach11：认为当前的AI代理在个人生活中的实用性有限，需要大量的信任和整合工作，Apple和Microsoft在这方面可能更有优势。
• Topfi：赞赏OpenAI在UI设计上的努力，认为其代理工具在视觉呈现和用户信息反馈方面做得很好，比其他实现更具吸引力。
• divan：希望AI代理能提供编辑文档的功能，特别是在项目中连续写作和语音模式的支持。
• dcre：对AI代理访问真实凭证和敏感信息的风险表示担忧。
• dcchambers：以幽默方式指出提示注入的风险，可能被利用来操纵用户行为。
• bryanhogan：一方面认为AI代理非常酷且可能有益，另一方面担心其深层次整合到系统中时可能犯的错误。
• serjester：认为OpenAI转向直接使用用户电脑是一个明智的策略，解决了Operator发布时面临的许多问题，特别是在网络封锁方面。
• jjcm：对LLM开始影响现实世界感到兴奋，认为这是LLM应用的一个重要时刻，并预测未来十年LLM将驱动很大一部分世界经济。
• ck2：以幽默方式指出使用ChatGPT生成大文档并下载可能带来的问题。

补充讨论：
• 安全性和隐私：多个评论提到了AI代理工具在处理个人数据和敏感信息时的安全风险，特别是提示注入和未经授权操作的问题。
• 错误处理：讨论了AI代理工具在处理复杂任务时可能犯的错误，特别是细微错误如何影响其可用性和用户信任。
• 用户体验：对OpenAI在UI设计和用户体验优化方面的努力给予了肯定，认为这可能吸引更多非开发者用户。
• 实用性和整合：讨论了AI代理工具在个人生活和工作中的实用性，以及与其他系统和平台的整合挑战。
• 未来发展：预测了AI代理工具在未来的应用潜力和可能面临的挑战。

data.title: Hungary's oldest library is fighting to save books from a beetle infestation
data.author: smollett
data.article_summary: 匈牙利最古老的潘诺恩哈尔马修道院图书馆正努力拯救约10万本手抄书，这些书受到甲虫侵扰。药店甲虫（也称面包甲虫）不仅出现在食物中，还被书籍的胶水和淀粉吸引。为消灭甲虫，修复人员将书籍放入密封塑料袋，抽空氧气，注入氮气，经过六周处理希望彻底消灭甲虫。处理后，每本书将逐一检查和吸尘，受损书籍将进行后续修复。虽然最古老和珍稀的书未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。

PANNONHALMA, Hungary — Tens of thousands of centuries-old books are being pulled from the shelves of a medieval abbey in Hungary in an effort to save them from a beetle infestation that could wipe out centuries of history.
Books We Love
NPR staffers pick their favorite fiction reads of 2025 so far
The 1,000-year-old Pannonhalma Archabbey is a sprawling Benedictine monastery that is one of Hungary's oldest centers of learning and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles burrowed into them.
The drugstore beetle, also known as the bread beetle, is often found among dried foodstuffs like grains, flour and spices. But they also are attracted to the gelatin and starch-based adhesives found in books.
Sponsor Message
They have been found in a section of the library housing around a quarter of the abbey's 400,000 volumes.
"This is an advanced insect infestation which has been detected in several parts of the library, so the entire collection is classified as infected and must be treated all at the same time," said Zsófia Edit Hajdu, the chief restorer on the project. "We've never encountered such a degree of infection before."
Abbey houses historical treasures
The beetle invasion was first detected during a routine library cleaning. Employees noticed unusual layers of dust on the shelves and then saw that holes had been burrowed into some of the book spines. Upon opening the volumes, burrow holes could be seen in the paper where the beetles chewed through.
The abbey at Pannonhalma was founded in 996, four years before the establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary. Sitting upon a tall hill in northwestern Hungary, the abbey houses the country's oldest collection of books, as well as many of its earliest and most important written records.
In this photo provided by Pannonhalma Archabbey, a restorer shows an old book with holes in its pages due to a drugstore beetle infestation, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3.
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
hide caption
toggle caption
AP/Pannonhalma Archabbey
For over 1,000 years, the abbey has been among the most prominent religious and cultural sites in Hungary and all of Central Europe, surviving centuries of wars and foreign incursions such as the Ottoman invasion and occupation of Hungary in the 16th century.
Sponsor Message
Ilona Ásványi, director of the Pannonhalma Archabbey library, said she is "humbled" by the historical and cultural treasures the collection holds whenever she enters.
"It is dizzying to think that there was a library here a thousand years ago, and that we are the keepers of the first book catalogue in Hungary," she said.
Performing Arts
Take a peek at Stephen Sondheim's papers, now at the Library of Congress
Among the library's most outstanding works are 19 codices, including a complete Bible from the 13th century. It also houses several hundred manuscripts predating the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century and tens of thousands of books from the 16th century.
While the oldest and rarest prints and books are stored separately and have not been infected, Ásványi said any damage to the collection represents a blow to cultural, historical and religious heritage.
"When I see a book chewed up by a beetle or infected in any other way, I feel that no matter how many copies are published and how replaceable the book is, a piece of culture has been lost," she said.
Books will spend weeks in an oxygen-free environment
To kill the beetles, the crates of books are being placed into tall, hermetically sealed plastic sacks from which all oxygen is removed. After six weeks in the pure nitrogen environment, the abbey hopes all the beetles will be destroyed.
Before being reshelved, each book will be individually inspected and vacuumed. Any book damaged by the pests will be set aside for later restoration work.
This photo provided by Pannonhalma Archabbey shows books kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary on July 3 as a beetle infestation threatens its ancient collection.

data.title: Ring introducing new feature to allow police to live-stream access to cameras
data.author: xoa
data.article_summary: Ring公司创始人Jamie Siminoff重新掌舵，并恢复了以监控为主、隐私为次的策略，重新引入允许警察直接向用户请求录像的功能，甚至新增允许警察实时访问家庭安全设备的功能。这一举措引发了对公民自由的严重威胁，因为警察曾利用Ring录像监视抗议者，且未经授权获取录像。Ring正在推翻过去几年进行的改革，包括恢复与警察的合作，并计划与Axon合作开发新工具，方便警察获取录像和实时流。此外，Ring计划转向“AI优先”，可能引入视频分析或面部识别技术。员工还被要求展示使用AI的证明以获得晋升。这一系列变化表明Ring正重回大规模监控工具的角色，可能是为了在技术威权主义崛起的背景下谋取利润。公众压力曾迫使Ring改进隐私措施，但现在这些进展正在被逆转。

44620002.article_content:
Ring founder Jamie Siminoff is
back at the helm
of the surveillance doorbell company, and with him is the
surveillance-first-privacy-last
approach that made Ring one of the most maligned tech devices. Not only is the company reintroducing new versions of old features which would allow police to request footage directly from Ring users, it is also introducing a new feature that would allow police to request live-stream access to people’s home security devices.
This is a bad, bad step for Ring and the broader public.
Ring is rolling back many of the reforms it’s made in the last few years by easing police access to footage from millions of homes in the United States. This is a grave threat to civil liberties in the United States. After all, police have used Ring footage to
spy
on protestors, and obtained footage
without a warrant or consent of the user
. It is easy to imagine that law enforcement officials will use their renewed access to Ring information to
find people who have had abortions
or track down people for
immigration enforcement
.
Siminoff has announced in a memo seen by
Business Insider
that the company will now be reimagined from the ground up to be “AI first”—whatever that means for a home security camera that lets you see who is ringing your doorbell. We fear that this may signal the introduction of video analytics or
face
recognition
to an already problematic surveillance device.
It was also reported that employees at Ring will have to show
proof that they use AI
in order to get promoted.
Not to be undone with new bad features, they are also planning on rolling back some of the necessary reforms Ring has made: namely
partnering with Axon
to build a new tool that would allow police to request Ring footage directly from users, and also allow users to consent to letting police livestream directly from their device.
After years of serving as the
eyes
and
ears
of police, the company was compelled by public pressure to make a number of necessary changes. They introduced
end-to-end encryption
, they ended their
formal partnerships with police
which were an
ethical minefield
, and they
ended their tool
that facilitated police requests for footage directly to customers. Now they are pivoting back to being a tool of mass surveillance.
Why now? It is hard to believe the company is betraying the trust of its millions of customers in the name of “safety” when violent crime in the United States is reaching
near-historically low levels
. It’s probably not about their customers—the
FTC had to compel
Ring to take its users’ privacy seriously.
No, this is most likely about Ring cashing in on the rising tide of techno-authoritarianism, that is, authoritarianism aided by surveillance tech. Too many tech companies want to profit from our shrinking liberties. Google likewise recently
ended an old ethical commitment
that prohibited it from profiting off of surveillance and warfare. Companies are locking down billion-dollar contracts by selling their products to the defense sector or police.
Shame on Ring.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：法律石碑是否在当时的法律实践中被实际运用

不同观点：
• 观点一（mcphage）：有历史学家提到，这些法律石碑尽管看起来很 impressive（令人印象深刻），但在当时的法律案件中并没有被实际引用。因此，这些石碑上的法律是“书写的法律”，而非“实践中的法律”。这个观点暗示了法律石碑可能更多是象征性或宣传性的，而非真正指导司法实践的文件。

补充讨论：
• 法律石碑的功能：mcphage 引用的观点质疑了这些法律石碑在当时社会中的实际法律效力，提出它们可能并不是用来指导司法判决的实际依据。
• 法律实践与书面法律的分离：这个观点指出了书面法律和实际法律操作之间可能存在差距，表明法律石碑可能只是统治者展示权力或合法性的一种方式。

争议焦点：
• 这些法律石碑是否真的没有在法律实践中使用过，或者只是历史记录中没有体现这一点，仍需要进一步考证。如果确实没有在实际案例中被引用，那么它们的主要功能和目的就变得更具讨论性，可能与权力展示、政治宣传等相关。

Engineers have created a new type of
robot
that places living fungi behind the controls.
The
biohybrid robot
uses electrical signals from an edible type of mushroom called a king trumpet in order to move around and sense its environment.
Developed by an interdisciplinary team from Cornell University in the US and Florence University in Italy, the machine could herald a new era of living robotics.
“Living systems respond to touch, they respond to light, they respond to heat, they respond to even some unknowns, like signals,” said Anand Mishra, a research associate in the Organic Robotics Lab at Cornell.
“That’s why we think, OK, if you wanted to build future
robots
, how can they work in an unexpected environment? We can leverage these living systems, and any unknown input comes in, the robot will respond to that.”
Researchers from Cornell University in the US and the University of Florence in Italy placed a species of edible mushroom within a robot body
(
Robert Shepherd
)
Different inputs, such as ultraviolet light, resulted in different outcomes for the way the robot moved. A video of one of the mushroom-controlled robots shows it moving slowly across a surface by pumping its robotic legs. Another biohybrid robot uses a wheeled system in order to move around.
Combining this mobility with the fungi’s ability to sense chemical and biological signals could prove useful in a range of applications, according to the researchers.
“By growing mycelium into the electronics of a robot, we were able to allow the biohybrid machine to sense and respond to the environment,” said Rob Shepherd, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at Cornell.
“The potential for future robots could be to sense soil chemistry in row crops and decide when to add more fertiliser, for example, perhaps mitigating downstream effects of agriculture like harmful algal blooms.”
Details of the biohybrid robot were published in the journal
Science Robotics
, in
a study
titled ‘Sensorimotor control of robots mediated by electro-physiological measurements of fungal mycelia’.
It is not the first time a living organism has been placed inside a robot body, though the use of mushrooms could offer a major breakthrough in the field of biohybrid robotics due to their ability to grow and survive in harsh conditions.
Previous experiments have included
an artificial worm brain placed inside a Lego robot
, which was able to recreate the creature’s movements and intentions.
Earlier this year, researchers from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) created a machine that was integrated with living muscle tissue in order to sense and adapt to its environment.

data.title: Intel to boost gross margins – new products must deliver 50% gross profit
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: Intel宣布将不再批准毛利率低于50%的新项目，以重振其利润率。CEO Lip-Bu Tan正推动公司毛利率重回50%以上，取消或调整不盈利项目，并可能进行多达20%的裁员。尽管公司整体尚未达到该目标，但未来项目如Panther Lake和Nova Lake预计将实现这一利润率。此举旨在提高盈利能力，但也引发内部对产品竞争力与成本结构的争论。Tan还计划通过裁减中层管理层和投资顶尖人才来重塑公司文化。这一策略获得投资者支持，但执行中面临挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：实验性研发与利润率之间的关系，以及企业如何应对利润率下降的问题。

不同观点：
• [0cf8612b2e1e] 认为，文章标题让他联想到通过宣布破产来试图改变现实的滑稽情景。他质疑实验性研发是否已经不再可行，并指出只有 incremental progress（渐进式进展）才能带来接近预期的利润率。该评论者对企业能否通过命令或意愿来直接提升利润率表示怀疑，暗示研发需要务实，可能更多地依赖小步改进。

• [Havoc] 则认为，利润率的下降是竞争力下降的结果，简单地命令高利润率并不能解决问题。他指出，企业竞争力的丧失是更深层次的问题，试图通过命令来提升利润率可能不会奏效。此外，他还提到GPU（图形处理单元）可能不是特别盈利，因此企业可能会削减这方面的业务。

补充讨论：
• [0cf8612b2e1e] 的评论带有一定的讽刺意味，通过引用《办公室》剧集中Michael Scott的台词，表达了对通过主观意愿改变现实的怀疑态度。
• [Havoc] 提到了竞争力和利润率之间的联系，认为利润率下降的根本原因在于竞争力的丧失，而不是研发策略的失误。他还推测企业可能会因为盈利问题而削减GPU业务，这可能对企业未来发展产生影响。
• 争议的焦点在于如何应对利润率下降的问题：一方认为应更加注重渐进式改进，另一方则认为应从根本上提升竞争力，而不是简单地追求高利润率。

总体来看，讨论围绕企业如何在利润率下降的情况下进行战略调整，特别是如何处理实验性研发和竞争力之间的关系。

44620774.article_content:
(Image credit: Intel)
Intel will not be entertaining any projects that do not promise to double its money going forward. Michelle Johnston Holthaus, CEO of Intel Products, announced at Bank of America's
global technology conference
that Intel is no longer approving new projects that cannot be proven to earn at least 50% gross margin "based on a set of industry expectations."
Holthaus explained Intel's new risk-averse policy as "something that we probably should have had before, but we have it now so that product doesn’t move forward; you actually don’t get engineers assigned to it if it’s not 50% or higher gross margins moving forward."
Holthaus also clarified that while Intel is not expecting or projecting 50% gross margins across all operations, it is a number the company is aspiring toward internally. All of Intel's future roadmap operations, including
Panther Lake
and
Nova Lake
, are also currently expected to reach the 50% gross profit number that the rest of the business aspires to.
You may like
Intel is not a top 10 chipmaker anymore, according to new CEO Lip-Bu Tan
Intel might axe the 18A process node for foundry customers, essentially leaving TSMC with no rival
Intel posts flat year-over-year earnings and bleak outlook, warns about macroeconomic pressures
The drive behind this initiative is reportedly coming from Intel's
new CEO
, Lip-Bu Tan. Tan is reportedly "laser focused on the fact that we need to get our gross margins back up above 50%." To accomplish this, Tan is also said to be investigating and potentially cancelling or changing unprofitable deals with other companies.
Intel's margins have slipped to new lows for the company in recent months.
MacroTrends
reports Intel's trailing 12 months gross margin for Q1 2025 was as low as 31.67%. Intel's gross margins had hovered around the 60% mark for the ten years leading up to the COVID-19 pandemic, falling beneath 50% in Q2 2022 and continuing to steadily fall ever since.
Holthaus predicts a "tug-of-war" to ensue within Intel in the coming months as engineers and executives reckon with being forced between a rock and a hard place. "We need to be building products that... fit the right competitive landscape and requirements of our customers, but also have the right cost structure in place. It really requires us to do both."
CEO Lip-Bu Tan has done much to streamline Intel's operation and right a rocking ship inherited from previous Intel chief Pat Gelsinger. Another
major round of layoffs
, potentially up to 20% of the remaining workforce, is coming in Q2, arriving after a major leadership change-up to remove middle management between Tan and other team leads.

Tan is also quoted as wanting to turn Intel into an "engineering-focused company" again under his leadership. To reach this, Tan has committed to investing in recruiting and retaining top talent; "I believe Intel has lost some of this talent over the years; I want to create a culture of innovation empowerment." Maintaining a culture of empowering innovation and top talent seems, on its face, at odds with layoffs and a lock on projects not projected to gross 50% margins, but Tan seemingly has Intel investors on his side in these pursuits.

data.title: Ask HN: What would convince you to take AI seriously?
data.author: atleastoptimal
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI的能力及其对社会的影响

不同观点：
• **exabrial**：认为AI不应该假装知道所有答案，避免像Reddit上的“专家”争论一样，过度自信地回答问题。应该坦诚自己的局限性。

• **al_borland**：AI不仅需要解决已知问题，还需要有能力创造未来。如果AI自动化所有人类劳动，社会结构需要大幅调整，否则会导致混乱。目前过度宣传AI取代人类是不负责任的。

• **andy99**：解决基准问题不代表真正的智能，AI需要展示真正的智能行为，而不仅仅是解决人为设定的有限问题。此外，当前的LLM（大语言模型）架构可能不足以支持真正的智能。

• **saadn92**：有些人不愿意适应AI的发展，但随着AI的广泛应用，他们将被迫适应。即使个人不喜欢AI，但它确实有其用途，现在不学习将来也得适应。

• **alganet**：认为讨论AI是否需要被重视是愚蠢的问题，没必要为此下结论。

• **mcphage**：对于开发工作，像DHH的“15分钟内建一个博客”演示那样的任务是可以的。对于原创性工作，AI应该解决一些知名的未解难题，例如Collatz猜想。

• **bigyabai**：AI如果能够替代真正的思维工作，其结果应该是显而易见的，特别是通过显著降低劳动成本体现出来。

• **noncoml**：不相信AI目前可以取代思维工作，认为AI目前只是一个辅助工具。真正的AI取代人类思维的时刻还未到来，大家到时自然会知道。

• **neximo64**：质疑为什么要认真对待AI，并反问为什么要提出这个问题。

补充讨论：
- AI是否能够创造未来和解决未知问题是讨论的焦点之一。
- AI对社会结构和劳动市场的潜在影响引发了一些人的担忧，尤其是自动化可能导致的混乱和痛苦。
- 对AI当前能力的评价存在分歧，有人认为它只是解决有限问题的工具，而有人则期待它展示真正的智能。
- 讨论中也存在对AI过度宣传的批评和对AI适应性的不同态度。

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种利用大型语言模型（LLMs）的多代理方法，以增强对COBOL代码的解释。COBOL因其复杂性和老旧，加上开发者减少，维护变得困难，尤其是缺乏文档。该方法使用两个LLM代理协作生成代码功能、文件及项目的解释，并结合上下文信息提升解释准确性。实验评估显示，该方法在函数和文件级别的解释上显著优于基准方法，尤其在处理超出LLM token限制的长代码时表现突出，并在项目级别成功解释了82%的项目功能和目的。

补充讨论：

Enhancing COBOL Code Explanations: A Multi-Agents Approach Using Large Language Models
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Enhancing COBOL Code Explanations: A Multi-Agents Approach Using Large Language Models, by Fangjian Lei and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Common Business Oriented Language (COBOL) is a programming language used to develop business applications that are widely adopted by financial, business, and government agencies. Due to its age, complexity, and declining number of COBOL developers, maintaining COBOL codebases is becoming increasingly challenging. In particular, the lack of documentation makes it difficult for new developers to effectively understand and maintain COBOL systems. Existing research utilizes large language models (LLMs) to explain the functionality of code snippets. However, COBOL presents unique challenges due to its architectural and syntactical differences, which often cause its code to exceed the token window size of LLMs. In this work, we propose a multi-agent approach that leverages two LLM-based agents working collaboratively to generate explanations for functions, files, and the overall project. These agents incorporate together by utilizing contextual information from the codebase into the code explanation prompts. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach using 14 open-source, real-world COBOL projects. Our results indicate that our approach performs significantly better than the baseline in function code explanation, with improvements of 12.67%, 18.59%, and 0.62% in terms of METEOR, chrF, and SentenceBERT scores, respectively. At the file level, our approach effectively explains both short and long COBOL files that exceed the token window size of LLMs and surpass the baseline by 4.21%, 10.72%, and 14.68% in explaining the purpose, functionality, and clarity of the generated explanation. At the project level, our approach generates explanations that convey the functionality and purpose of 82% of the selected projects.

data.title: Meta says it won't sign Europe AI agreement
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Meta Platforms拒绝签署欧盟的人工智能行为准则，认为该准则过度监管，将阻碍公司发展。全球事务主管Joel Kaplan表示，该准则引入了诸多法律不确定性，超出了欧盟《人工智能法》的范围。该法旨在提升技术透明度和安全性，但Kaplan批评欧洲在AI监管上走错方向。此前，欧洲委员会发布了最终版准则，由企业自行决定是否签署。ASML Holding和Airbus等公司也曾反对该准则，呼吁推迟两年实施，而OpenAI则已承诺签署。Kaplan今年取代Nick Clegg担任现职。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟人工智能法案（AI Act）及其自愿行为守则的实施和影响

不同观点：
• **反对推迟实施的观点**：一些评论（如[jahewson], [isodev]）认为，尽管法规可能繁琐，但它们对于保护版权和规范AI使用是必要的。尤其是[isodev]提到，作为公民，支持AI法案，因为需要对技术巨头施加限制以保护人类利益。

• **支持推迟实施的观点**：[ankit219], [cakealert]等人认为，法案和行为守则的实施不够明确，可能导致过度的监管负担，尤其是对开源模型的责任要求过于严格。他们指出，40家欧盟公司要求推迟两年实施，因为需要更多时间来适应法规。[cakealert]还提到，AI发展的势头无法阻挡，法规可能无法有效干预。

• **对Meta立场的批评和质疑**：[rchaud], [mediumsmart]等评论质疑Meta反对法案的动机，认为Meta只是为了保护其自身增长，而不是出于对法规合理性的关切。他们指出，Meta的反对缺乏具体说明什么是令人反感的政策。

• **对法规具体影响的担忧**：[throwpoaster], [chvid]等担心法规会导致不必要的繁文缛节，比如在所有LLM中添加弹出提示，类似于网站上的cookies弹窗。此外，[chvid]质疑Meta为何需要签署自愿协议，既然欧盟法律已经要求在其境内运营的公司遵守。

• **对Meta和欧盟公司利益的讨论**：[sorokod], [paulddraper]提到Meta关注欧洲公司的增长问题，担心法案会限制前沿AI模型的发展。同时，[paulddraper]指出OpenAI已经承诺签署自愿行为守则，显示不同公司对法规的不同态度。

补充讨论：
• **对法规制定透明度的关注**：[vanderZwan]承认自己对AI协议的偏见，因为不了解具体内容而难以判断其实际影响。
• **对法规措辞的建议**：[chrisweekly]指出新闻中对Meta立场的描述存在措辞歧义，建议使用连字符以避免误解。

争议焦点：法案的实施是否过于繁琐和严格，是否会阻碍AI技术的创新与发展，以及Meta反对法案的真实动机。

data.title: Asynchrony is not concurrency
data.author: kristoff_it
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了异步（asynchrony）、并发（concurrency）和并行（parallelism）之间的区别，强调了异步并不等同于并发。作者指出，异步是指任务可以不按顺序执行但仍保持正确性，而并发是指系统能够同时推进多个任务。在Zig语言中，异步并不意味着并发，因为使用`io.async`并不强制要求并发执行，可以在单线程阻塞模式下运行。这种区分有助于更精确地描述代码行为，并解决编程生态中因概念混淆导致的问题，如库作者的重复工作、用户必须放弃同步代码等。明确异步与并发的区别能改善编程体验，避免不必要的复杂性和潜在的死锁问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于async和并发（concurrency）的定义和实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• Yoric认为，async意味着代码为并发结构化，但async代码中仍然可能出现用户导致的竞态条件（race conditions）。他指出，async并不自动等同于正确性，并发问题依然存在。
• jayd16认为，将"让出执行权"（yielding execution）从并发的定义中分离出来并创造新的"异步"（asynchrony）术语会增加困惑。他认为并发本质上包含了让出执行权的概念。
• kazinator指出，异步是一种抽象，它将请求的提交和结果的收集分离开来，允许但不强制并发实现。他强调，异步的动机在于获得并发带来的好处，某些异步抽象无法在单线程中实现。
• reichstein认为，异步在单线程、合作式多任务（cooperative multitasking）环境下有意义，而在多线程或并发执行模型中则不需要异步，因为可以使用阻塞I/O。
• kobzol担心Zig的新I/O设计在库的编写中可能导致错误，因为库作者无法确定I/O是单线程还是多线程，是否使用事件I/O。他们认为在广泛的I/O实现中编写并发/异步代码将非常困难，需要防御性编程。
• t43562指出，异步代码的测试难度大，难以确保所有可能的生产场景都已覆盖。他们还提到，多线程程序更难写和调试，需要小心处理。

补充讨论：
• threatofrain认为，作者在并发的定义上混淆了概念，并引用了一篇论文来支持其观点。
• jlouis提出，通过测试异步术语在多种语言和并发设计中的有用性来判断其必要性。
• dvt认为，"异步"是一个糟糕的词汇，建议使用更精确的数学术语"交换性"（commutativity）。他们认为现有的异步编程范式令人困惑，不如使用已经熟悉的模式。
• northhnbesthn批评文章过于复杂，认为工具和实现有问题。
• nemothekid对Zig中无栈协程的实现方式感到困惑，并担心FFI可能导致阻塞系统调用。
• tossandthrow指出，文章没有提及并发中的一些陷阱，如执行非幂等函数多次时需要互斥锁。
• danaugrs对Zig即将推出的异步I/O表示期待。
• butterisgood通过日常生活中的例子解释了异步和并发的区别，并指出它们不同于并行。
• skybrian认为，库在不同环境中的可移植性是重要的，类型系统可以帮助捕获函数调用中的错误。

争议焦点：
• 异步和并发之间的关系及定义是主要争议点。Yoric、jayd16和kazinator等人在此问题上存在不同见解。
• Zig的新I/O设计是否实用、是否会导致库编写困难也是讨论中的争议点。

Asynchrony is not Concurrency
July 18, 2025
•
12
min read • by
Loris Cro
Yes I know about that one talk from Rob Pike.
The title of this blog post is not something you hear people say often, if ever. What you do hear people say is “concurrency is not parallelism”, but that’s not as useful, in my opinion.
Let’s see how Wikipedia defines those terms:
Concurrency
refers to the ability of a system to execute multiple tasks through simultaneous execution or time-sharing (context switching)
Parallel computing
is a type of computation in which many calculations or processes are carried out simultaneously.
What if I told you we’re missing a term to describe another aspect of concurrent programming and, because of it, we’re all collectively missing a key piece of understanding that has shaped our software ecosystems for the worse?
Well, I spoiled it in the title: the missing term is ‘asynchrony’, but why?
Two files
Say that you have to save two files and order does not matter:
io
.
async
(
saveFileA
,
.
{
io
}
)
;
io
.
async
(
saveFileB
,
.
{
io
}
)
;
A could be saved before B, or B could be saved before A, and all would be fine. You could also write
some of
A, then
some of
B, and then back to A, to finally complete writing B. That also would be correct, and in fact that’s what tends to happen when using evented I/O to save sufficiently complex files concurrently.
But, most importantly,
it’s perfectly legitimate to do all the work to save one file first and, only once that’s done, to begin saving the second file
. Maybe that would not be the most efficient thing to do, but the code would still be correct.
Two sockets
Let’s take a look now at another example: say that you need to create a TCP server and connect to it
from within the same program
.
// assume that server.listen has already been called
io
.
async
(
Server
.
accept
,
.
{
server
,
io
}
)
;
io
.
async
(
Client
.
connect
,
.
{
client
,
io
}
)
;
Like before, the order doesn’t matter: the client could begin a connection before the server starts accepting (the OS will buffer the client request in the meantime), or the server could start accepting first and wait for a bit before seeing an incoming connection.
Unlike before,
it is mandatory that the execution of both tasks overlap
.
In the file example it was fine to do all the work for A first and all the work for B last, but not in this second case, because the server needs to be active
while
the client tries to connect.
Asynchrony, Concurrency, Parallelism
In common lingo, we would describe both the code snippets presented above as “concurrent” and stop there, but that will lose us some nuance, so here’s my proposed definitions for these terms:
Asynchrony
: the possibility for tasks to run out of order and still be correct.
Concurrency
: the ability of a system to progress multiple tasks at a time, be it via parallelism or task switching.
Parallelism
: the ability of a system to execute more than one task simultaneously at the physical level.
With these definitions in hand, here’s a better description of the two code snippets from before: both scripts express asynchrony, but the second one
requires
concurrency.
Why even bother?
Ok, cool, we now can be more precise when describing code snippets, so what did we gain?
For dramatic effect, allow me to answer this question in the negative and tell you what it is that we lost by not being aware enough of the difference between asynchrony and concurrency.
Because of our lack of understanding:
We have created language ecosystems where library authors must duplicate effort (e.g.
redis-py
vs
asyncio-redis
) or
worse
.
We have created a
worse
experience
for library users where async code is viral and where a even a single dependency with async code demands that users give up their ability to write normal, synchronous code.
And to mitigate all these problems, we have created unholy escape hatches that cause suboptimal behavior at best and
deadlocks
at worst.
Let’s switch back to answering the question in the positive.
In Zig Asynchrony is not Concurrency
I already wrote a blog post on
Zig’s new async I/O
story, but I only dedicated a short section at the end on this aspect, which led me to expand on it in this post.
In Zig asynchrony is not concurrency because the usage of
io.async
does not imply concurrency. In other words: code that uses
io.async
can be run in single-threaded blocking mode.
Let’s look again at the file example:
io
.
async
(
saveFileA
,
.
{
io
}
)
;
io
.
async
(
saveFileB
,
.
{
io
}
)
;
When run in single-threaded blocking mode, the code above will be equivalent to this:
saveFileA
(
io
)
;
saveFileB
(
io
)
;
It’s easy to imagine how this can be done, all
io.async
has to do is run the given function immediately (instead of spawning a new thread for it, or doing any other form of task switching).
This means that a library author can use
io.async
in their code and not force their users
44608754.article_summary: 本文讨论了异步（asynchrony）、并发（concurrency）和并行（parallelism）之间的区别，强调了异步并不等同于并发。作者指出，异步是指任务可以不按顺序执行但仍保持正确性，而并发是指系统能够同时推进多个任务。在Zig语言中，异步并不意味着并发，因为使用`io.async`并不强制要求并发执行，可以在单线程阻塞模式下运行。这种区分有助于更精确地描述代码行为，并解决编程生态中因概念混淆导致的问题，如库作者的重复工作、用户必须放弃同步代码等。明确异步与并发的区别能改善编程体验，避免不必要的复杂性和潜在的死锁问题。
44608754.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于async和并发（concurrency）的定义和实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• Yoric认为，async意味着代码为并发结构化，但async代码中仍然可能出现用户导致的竞态条件（race conditions）。他指出，async并不自动等同于正确性，并发问题依然存在。
• jayd16认为，将"让出执行权"（yielding execution）从并发的定义中分离出来并创造新的"异步"（asynchrony）术语会增加困惑。他认为并发本质上包含了让出执行权的概念。
• kazinator指出，异步是一种抽象，它将请求的提交和结果的收集分离开来，允许但不强制并发实现。他强调，异步的动机在于获得并发带来的好处，某些异步抽象无法在单线程中实现。
• reichstein认为，异步在单线程、合作式多任务（cooperative multitasking）环境下有意义，而在多线程或并发执行模型中则不需要异步，因为可以使用阻塞I/O。
• kobzol担心Zig的新I/O设计在库的编写中可能导致错误，因为库作者无法确定I/O是单线程还是多线程，是否使用事件I/O。他们认为在广泛的I/O实现中编写并发/异步代码将非常困难，需要防御性编程。
• t43562指出，异步代码的测试难度大，难以确保所有可能的生产场景都已覆盖。他们还提到，多线程程序更难写和调试，需要小心处理。

补充讨论：
• threatofrain认为，作者在并发的定义上混淆了概念，并引用了一篇论文来支持其观点。
• jlouis提出，通过测试异步术语在多种语言和并发设计中的有用性来判断其必要性。
• dvt认为，"异步"是一个糟糕的词汇，建议使用更精确的数学术语"交换性"（commutativity）。他们认为现有的异步编程范式令人困惑，不如使用已经熟悉的模式。
• northhnbesthn批评文章过于复杂，认为工具和实现有问题。
• nemothekid对Zig中无栈协程的实现方式感到困惑，并担心FFI可能导致阻塞系统调用。
• tossandthrow指出，文章没有提及并发中的一些陷阱，如执行非幂等函数多次时需要互斥锁。
• danaugrs对Zig即将推出的异步I/O表示期待。
• butterisgood通过日常生活中的例子解释了异步和并发的区别，并指出它们不同于并行。
• skybrian认为，库在不同环境中的可移植性是重要的，类型系统可以帮助捕获函数调用中的错误。

争议焦点：
• 异步和并发之间的关系及定义是主要争议点。Yoric、jayd16和kazinator等人在此问题上存在不同见解。
• Zig的新I/O设计是否实用、是否会导致库编写困难也是讨论中的争议点。

data.title: HathiTrust Digital Library
data.author: djoldman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HathiTrust与Google Books的比较及其在公共领域作品访问上的优势，以及HathiTrust的技术背景、使用体验和应用场景。

不同观点：
• **philipkglass**：HathiTrust在允许访问美国公共领域作品方面比Google Books做得更好。HathiTrust对许多20世纪作品的版权状态进行了更复杂的清理，而Google Books似乎只遵循1929年前的简单规则。虽然Google Books的搜索界面更快更好，但HathiTrust提供了更多可阅读的公共领域内容。此外，Google的扫描带有下载限制，只有与学术图书馆相关的人才能下载整本书，但公众可以逐页下载。

• **roadside_picnic**：HathiTrust诞生于2002-2010年间的图书馆技术黄金时期，当时由于互联网泡沫破裂，许多技术人才因兴趣而非高薪加入图书馆项目。这一时期产生了大量创新项目，但随着2010年后科技行业崛起和预算削减，这种现象逐渐消失。

• **robin_reala**：HathiTrust作为Standard Ebooks的扫描来源非常有用，尽管Archive.org的界面更好，但HathiTrust的选择更广泛。

• **acidburnNSA**：作为一名核能历史学家，HathiTrust是一个非常有价值的资源，提供了大量资料，且多年来一直表现出色。

• **dilawar**：指出HathiTrust的名称在 Hindi 中的含义（大象），并对该平台非印度背景但位于美国感到好奇。

• **leetrout**：其家庭来自肯塔基州东部，通过在公立大学的经历访问了HathiTrust和纽约公共图书馆，发现其中有许多有趣的内容。注意到几年前公开可用的内容没有现在多。

• **apaprocki**：经常使用HathiTrust进行家谱研究，虽然数据集共享方式复杂，但许多内容在其他地方找不到。

• **TZubiri**：通过国会图书馆获得HathiTrust的法律信息链接，快速且免费，体验非常好。

• **pyuser583**：认为HathiTrust是一个优秀资源，应该更加普及。

补充讨论：
• HathiTrust的技术背景和其在图书馆技术黄金时期的发展历程是roadside_picnic关注的焦点，强调了技术人才在图书馆项目中的作用及其变化。
• 多个评论提到HathiTrust在公共领域和学术研究中的实用性，尤其是在历史、法律和家谱研究中的具体应用。
• 争议焦点之一是Google Books和HathiTrust在公共领域作品访问上的限制和用户体验差异，philipkglass指出了Google Books下载限制的问题。
• 也有评论关注HathiTrust的普及程度和其名称的文化背景。

data.author: sjuut
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讲述了一次艰难的数据恢复过程，涉及从任天堂工厂用于Wii和Wii U系统的GameCube记忆卡和SD卡中恢复数据。这些卡片曾被任天堂压坏以销毁数据，但作者成功恢复了其中一部分数据。约50%的记忆卡因损坏严重无法恢复，25%通过简单修理恢复了数据，剩下的25%则需要通过焊接等复杂手段修复。文章还提到了一种通过Wii U的boot1漏洞实现的新型破解方法。此外，作者详细描述了在SD卡上使用TSOP 48夹具进行NAND芯片数据恢复的挑战，包括卡片极易受热变形以及焊接难度极高等问题。最终，作者成功完成了一次数据恢复，但在多次使用后设备出现故障。

44609479.article_content:
Preface: I am going to speak mostly in regards to my hand in this as I don’t have solid understanding of the Wii U software and architecture and I don’t want to throw out incorrect information. Where needed I have provided quotes and screenshots so that the information provided is coming straight from the horses mouth.
Data recovery
Recently I have had the pleasure to work with an amazing and talented group of people. It starts off like this.
WiiCurious contacted me asking if I might possibly be able to recover some data from GameCube Memory Cards and SD Cards that were used in the Nintendo factory setup process for installing the software to the Wii and Wii U systems, respectively. Nintendo tried to destroy these Memory Cards and SD Cards by crushing them and bending them in the middle. By doing so, Nintendo did damage about 50% of the Memory Cards to the point that the main flash memory IC was busted and the die was broken, so no hope. About 25% of the cards were still functional with a little straightening and convincing and I was able to recover the data. The last 25% of the Memory Cards required some sort of soldering or rework to recover the data, most of them being that the PCB was damaged and the flash IC needed to be placed on a good working board. It was laboring work, but much important and never before seen data was recovered. There were a couple of cards where the pins were broken off the flash IC and they required dremeling and some cutesy soldering tricks to pull off.
Factory GameCube Memory Cards Dumps
for anyone interested.
Kelly was having her own hand in recovering data from Memory Cards and SD Cards as well and did some rather impressive work.
But this is not what this post is about. What we are talking about today is the new Wii U exploit discovered by legendary developer Rairii. This exploit takes advantage of a boot1 vulnerability that allows for code to be run from the SD Card upon boot.
Why did I go on this rant about data recovery of Memory Cards and SD Cards? Because WiiCurious got a great idea. The SD Cards that he sent me, about 25% of them had their NAND flash IC broken, but the other 75% only sustained damage to the PCB.
I have become known for my tricks with putting TSOP 48 clips on Wii’s and other devices so I can swap out the NAND chips on devices for external programming and repair. Well, these Toshiba 2GB SD Cards that Nintendo used a lot of in the Wii U factory process have TSOP 48 NAND flash IC’s. We tried to remove the NAND flash chips and dump the data with an external programmer, but none of the programmer devices that we have can work with NAND flash chips of that size. We would have to buy newer expensive devices to do so. Not only that, but the data placed on the NAND flash IC’s was manipulated by the SD Card’s controller chip, thus the data dumped directly from the NAND would not be a direct representation of what would be on the SD Card.
And this is where WiiCurious asked why don’t we just put a TSOP 48 clip onto a known good and working SD card in place of the NAND chip, and then we can easily just swap out the NAND chip. And with that, WiiCurious send me a handful of donor SD Cards and a few TSOP 48 clips.
I can not express how incredibly difficult it is to solder these TSOP 48 clips on to anything at all. They melt at a rather lower temperature. If the solder is melted, then the plastic of these will be soft and malleable. In most cases the solder pads of the PCB are the same size as the pins of the clip, making it impossibly difficult to see even with magnification. To solder these on you must tin the pads of the PCB first, then place the TSOP 48 clip directly on top of the peaks of the tinned pads. Finally you must reflow the solder. The right way to do it would be with a reflow oven and using solder paste with a stencil, but I do not have those. I do have my infrared preheater which works well enough for these things.
But these SD Cards posed an extra unique challenge. The PCB’s are very thin and they bend easily and can warp with heat. Not only that, but most of these donor SD Cards were already warped to begin with. I had to carefully select the ones that I thought could be most viable and do what I could. The other consideration is that the controller chips is a direct die on PCB with a black blob. I have a feeling that those also are susceptible to damage from heat and warping.
With that said, my first attempt was successful and I was able to dump eight NAND flash IC’s using it before it started showing signs of failure. I expected these to not have a long shelf life because to latch and unlatch these TSOP 48 clips requires a bit of force, and with how thin and flexible the PCB’s are, I knew that they would not last long. I did try to mitigate this with some hot glue, which I believed help prolong the life a little. And luckily, since I did only use hot glue, I should be able to easily remove it and reflow the PCB again and hopefully fix it if it is ju

data.title: How I keep up with AI progress
data.author: itzlambda
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了生成式AI技术的快速发展及其普遍的误解。许多公司和政府推出了有缺陷甚至危险的AI产品，主要由于对AI技术的不了解导致误用。常见的误解包括低估（认为AI只是暂时的 hype）和高估（认为不再需要程序员）。构建对AI的清晰理解非常具有挑战性，因为信息环境中充斥着误导内容。作者提供了一份经过筛选的信息来源列表，帮助读者建立平衡和健康的理解，包括Simon Willison的博客、Andrej Karpathy的视频、以及各大AI实验室的官方公告和论文。作者建议直接从可信的原始来源获取信息，并关注一些在AI领域有深度见解的专家评论。

44608275.article_content:
Atharva Raykar
Read more by Atharva
here
Last Updated: 30th June 2025
Generative AI has been the fastest moving technology I have seen in my lifetime. Its also happens to be terribly misunderstood.
We have already seen large
companies
and even
governments
ship dysfunctional or even
dangerous
AI products. Sufficiently uninformed people
misunderstand how to apply AI
with concretely negative consequences.
The most common errors of misunderstanding are either underestimation (“it’s all hype that will blow over”) or overestimation (“I don’t need programmers anymore”). These patterns are rooted in a lack of a solid understanding of the technology and how it is evolving over time.
It’s surprisingly challenging to build a clear understanding of AI. We are in one of the most polluted information environments. If you’re not being deliberate about it, you are likely exposed to a lot of misinformation that overstates or dismisses AI capabilities.
To help with this, I’ve curated a list of sources that make up an information pipeline that I consider balanced and healthy. If you’re late to the game, consider this a good starting point.
Table of Contents
General guidelines
Starting Points
Simon Willison’s Blog
Andrej Karpathy
Every’s Chain of Thought
Official announcements, blogs and papers from those building AI
High signal people to follow
Hamel Husain
Shreya Shankar
Jason Liu
Eugene Yan
What We’ve Learned From A Year of Building with LLMs
Chip Huyen
Omar Khattab
Kwindla Hultman Kramer
Han Chung Lee
Jo Kristian Bergum
David Crawshaw
Alexander Doria / Pierre Carl-Langlais
Nathan Lambert’s “Interconnects”
Ethan Mollick
Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor’s “AI Snake Oil”
News and Media
Twitter / X
Shawn Wang aka swyx / AI news by smol.ai
Dwarkesh Patel
Esoterica
LessWrong / AI Alignment Forum
Gwern
Prompt Whisperers and Latent space explorers
Do I chug water from a firehose?
General guidelines
Stay close to the source. The further you stray from reading official announcements and write-ups from the AI labs, the more likely you are going to be exposed to noise. Always assume that all reporting is wrong by default, unless it’s coming from the primary source, or one of the people listed here.
Follow trustworthy individuals for commentary. I have linked to many individuals who talk about AI developments in good faith and engage with a deep sense of curiosity.
Starting Points
Simon Willison’s Blog (
link
)
The best starting point for most technical people. If I had to only pick one stream of information, it would be this one.
He’s also known for creating Django and Datasette.
Expect:
Commentary on the frontier of AI capabilities.
Application layer use cases.
Commentary on security issues and ethics.
A sample:
The Lethal Trifecta
,
LLMs in 2024
Andrej Karpathy (
Twitter
and
YouTube
)
Director of AI @ Tesla, founding member of OpenAI.
The best starting point to get an overview of how the models themselves work. His 3.5 hour video is the best million feet overview on the internals of LLMs and surprisingly approachable for relatively non-technical people too.
Expect:
Commentary on the frontier of AI capabilities
Approachable explanations on the internals of AI (I haven’t gone through all of these yet, but heard praise for his GPT-2 from scratch and zero to hero tutorials)
Strong cultural influence and observations on AI impact. He coined the terms “vibe coding” and “jagged intelligence”.
A sample:
Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
,
How I Use LLMs
Every’s Chain of Thought (
link
)
Written by Dan Shipper, the co-founder of Every. I like going through their test runs of the latest frontier models. It’s also a good way to get a sense of how these AI models can be used everyday.
Expect:
Practical applications of AI at work.
Vibe-checks for model capabilities outside of benchmark numbers.
A sample:
Vibe Check: Codex
,
Vibe Check: o3
Official announcements, blogs and papers from those building AI
Even though these labs sometimes get a bad rap for hyping up AI capabilities, their official announcements have a lot of valuable and generally accurate information on the capabilities of AI.
Always look out for the announcements from
OpenAI
,
Google DeepMind
,
Anthropic
,
DeepSeek
,
Meta AI
,
xAI
and
Qwen
.
Most labs usually have a bunch of useful resources that help deepen your understanding of LLM capabilities.
Announcement blog posts for an overview
Example:
OpenAI o3 announcement post
.
Official engineering blogs, guides and cookbooks
Examples:
Engineering at Anthropic
,
OpenAI’s voice agent guide
,
Gemini Cookbook
System/Model Cards for more details on the models—expect more detailed information on context windows, benchmarks, safety testing, etc
Example:
Claude 4 System Card
Research Papers
Examples:
DeepSeek R1’s paper about RL
,
Anthropic’s On the Biology of a Large Language Model
If you see anyone making an explosive claim about capabilities, or quoting some research from these labs, I always bypass the person making the claim and read i

data.title: Inspect ANSI control codes and escape sequences
data.author: webpro
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了多个与文件管理、数据显示和命令执行相关的技术概念和工具。主要包括：使用`ls`和`eza`命令列出文件块（blocks），进行测试运行（test run），处理超链接（hyperlinks），理解八进制（octal）和8位数据表示，执行命令（commands），应用不同样式（styles）和颜色（colors），管理行列（rows, columns），反转显示（invert），网格布局（grid），计数（count），处理重复项（duplicates），排序（sort），代码助记符（mnemonic），描述生成，纯文本处理，映射位置（map position），以及处理换行符和贪婪算法等。这些工具和概念常用于文件管理、数据处理和终端操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ANSI控制字符、终端 escape 序列的处理和调试工具

不同观点：
• SpaceL10n分享了一次因为未处理的ANSI控制字符导致搜索页面崩溃的调试经历，强调了数据清理的重要性。
• webpro介绍了一个用于检查和可视化ANSI控制代码的网络工具，并邀请反馈以改进工具。
• tronster表示对ANSI的魅力有特殊情感，提到现代操作系统对颜色支持的限制，以及缺乏好的ANSI编辑器。
• 112233对工具中SGR未按名称调用表示困惑，质疑工具在极端情况下的有效性。
• mnurzia指出工具在处理原始ESC字符时的不足，建议增加对这类字符的支持。
• taviso推荐了另一个调试工具sequin，认为在终端中调试更方便。
• ryan-c表示正在实验终端escape序列，并愿意合作进一步研究。
• JdeBP详细讨论了“ANSI”术语的误用，强调了ECMA标准的重要性，并指出了在处理控制序列时的常见错误和复杂性。
• gwbas1c表达了对编写ANSI解析器的兴趣，源于对BBS时代的怀念。
• codesnik好奇哪些编程语言对"\u001b"有美观的表示。
• FlyingAvatar表示在1993年时会非常需要这样的工具。
• imran9m发现该工具对美化Jenkins CI输出有用。
• teddyh指出工具不支持文本闪烁功能。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个工具和资源，如webpro的网络工具、taviso的sequin工具，以及JdeBP提到的详细技术文档和历史背景。
• 争议焦点在于工具的有效性和全面性，特别是对极端情况和不同终端行为的支持。
• JdeBP对“ANSI”术语的误用进行了学术性的纠正，强调了ECMA标准在控制序列处理中的重要性。
• 对现代操作系统和终端在颜色支持和控制序列处理方面的不足进行了讨论。
• 对工具的改进建议包括增加对原始ESC字符的支持和实现更全面的控制序列解码功能。
